Submission Instructions

  1. Assemble your comprehensive TEI P5 master document containing: full <teiHeader> with cataloguing and <editorialDecl>; diplomatic facsimile links; consensus normalized reading text; critical apparatus (<app>); morphological markup (<w>); translation alignment; and scholarly commentary notes.
  2. Execute the 12-gate quality assurance verification sweep (schema validation, pointer integrity, zero lint issues).
  3. Compile the multi-modal outputs: an interactive offline HTML edition and a formatted PDF volume via CSS Paged Media.
  4. Include a LICENSE.md explicitly specifying your multi-tiered licensing (e.g. CC BY 4.0 for edition text, CC0 for metadata, MIT for custom scripts).
  5. Submit your complete edition ZIP repository and a 300–500 word final editorial statement reflecting on how digital methods fundamentally altered your understanding of your primary historical witness.
